title: What Is a Sub-Merchant? KYC, Onboarding and Payment Aggregator Models
summary: Learn what a sub-merchant is, how sub-merchant KYC works in India, and how payment aggregator models and merchant onboarding APIs support platforms.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


As a platform business, to get new merchants online, you need to onboard them. The process of adding new merchants to your payment processing platform is called sub-merchant onboarding. How fast merchants can go live with your program is directly tied to how well you do sub-merchant onboarding. It is also tied to how well you keep your payment program safe.


This article defines a sub-merchant and explains how the Indian payment aggregator (PA) model functions. It describes the differences between the PA model and the payment facilitator (PF) model. Additionally, it details the applicable know your customer (KYC) requirements, and how using a merchant onboarding API can streamline the entire process.


### Key Takeaways


- A sub-merchant accepts payments through an intermediary arrangement. Its exact contractual relationship depends on the programme.
- PayFac is a card-network programme role; a payment aggregator is an RBI-regulated category in India.
- Sub-merchant KYC depends on business type, ownership and the applicable due diligence route. Smaller-merchant provisions do not remove verification.
- A merchant onboarding API connects profile creation, KYC, status tracking and activation within your product. A created profile is not an approved merchant.


##


What Is a Sub-Merchant?


A sub-merchant is a merchant who sells goods or services and accepts payments via an intermediary arrangement with a payment provider. In a PayFac programme, this generally means the merchant does not have their own direct merchant account. For example: booking platforms, ERPs (enterprise resource planning), marketplaces etc. have payment arrangements; whereas merchants/vendors on these websites (sub-merchants) receive money from customers via them.


Each sub-merchant receives a unique identifier used in transactions so that when reports are generated and/or payments settled, each transaction is linked to the proper merchant. However, a sub-merchant identifier is not considered an independent direct merchant account. Sub-merchants remain independently accountable for all aspects relating to genuine sales, delivery/fulfillment, refund requests/customer support and their contractual obligations.


The term does not describe every platform arrangement in exactly the same way. In our Embedded Payments flow, businesses are registered as merchants in Cashfree’s system and linked to the platform’s partner account.


##


How the Payment Aggregator Model Works in India


The Indian[payment aggregator model](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/payment-aggregators/) collects customer payments for merchants and settles those funds to the merchant. The Reserve Bank of India regulates payment aggregators. On September 15, 2025, the RBI issued its[Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregators](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12896) , which categorises PAs into three types:


- **PA-O (online):** At the time of the transaction, the acceptance device and payment instrument are not present in close proximity to each other.
- **PA-P (physical):** At the time of the transaction, both the acceptance device and payment instrument are physically present in close proximity to each other.
- **PA-CB (cross-border):** Cross-border payments are facilitated for permissible current account transactions through e-commerce.


Non-bank payment aggregators must maintain a minimum net worth of ₹15 crore at the time of application. Non-bank payment aggregators must maintain a minimum net worth of ₹25 crore by the end of their third financial year after receiving authorization. Payment aggregators must comply with applicable PMLA/AML obligations. Non-bank PAs must register with FIU-IND and meet the applicable reporting requirements. Merchant collections are held in a separate escrow account with a scheduled commercial bank; settlement follows the applicable rules and the PA and merchant agreement.


For platforms, this creates opportunities for platforms to form partnerships with authorised payment aggregators. These partnerships allow platforms to embed payment acceptance for their merchants. The payment aggregator will be responsible for its regulated activities, including due diligence and settling accounts according to relevant regulations. A platform’s own authorisation requirements depend on its activities and fund flow; a partnership is not a blanket exemption.


##


Payment Facilitator vs Payment Aggregator: What Is the Difference?


Both terms are commonly used in the industry; however, they describe different regulatory and programme roles. Their services may overlap.


A payment facilitator (PayFac) is a role within programmes offered by card networks. Through card network and acquiring bank programmes, PayFacs are approved to onboard qualified businesses as sub-merchants under a sponsored merchant agreement. The sponsoring acquiring bank is responsible for overseeing the programme.


A payment aggregator is a regulated category in India. Authorised payment aggregators must follow RBI guidelines regarding merchant onboarding, escrow requirements and governance.


**Model** **Originated from** **Overseen by** **Functionality**


PayFac Card-network and acquiring-bank programmes Sponsor acquiring bank and applicable card-network rules Allows qualified businesses to be onboarded as sponsored sub-merchants


Payment aggregator (India) RBI regulations Reserve Bank of India Collects payments for merchants and settles funds to them


##


Who Is Responsible for Sub-Merchant Onboarding and Payments?


Any type of aggregator or facilitation arrangement includes a split of responsibilities. Liability is defined by applicable law, network rules and the agreements entered into by the parties involved.


Typically, the payment provider is responsible for sub-merchant onboarding, due diligence, transaction monitoring, dispute operations, applicable reserves and reporting. The acquiring bank, if applicable, sponsors and oversees the programme.


Sub-merchants remain liable for legitimate transactions made by them including sales fulfillment, returns/refunds, and customer service.


When acting as a platform, read your agreements. Be aware of which party pays out should you lose a dispute, which party retains reserves, and who contacts the merchant in the event something does go wrong.


##


How Does Sub-Merchant Onboarding Work?


Each program is unique; however, sub-merchant onboarding typically follows this process:


1. **Gathering information:** The platform collects business information and[banking details](https://www.cashfree.com/bank-account-verification/) about the merchant.
2. **Due diligence:** The provider verifies the merchant’s identity and assesses risks associated with their business.
3. **Onboarding:** Once vetted, the approved merchants are enabled and able to accept payments.
4. **Transaction processing and settlement:** Funds received via payments are processed and settled to each merchant’s designated bank account according to the applicable arrangement.
5. **Continuous monitoring:** Transactions are continuously monitored for potential fraud/dispute activity or other irregularities.


Automation allows faster onboarding processes; however, high-risk or incomplete applications may require manual reviews. Plan accordingly.


##


Sub-Merchant KYC and RBI Due Diligence Requirements


For all new merchants onboarded from January 1, 2026, the RBI’s merchant due diligence rules apply. The PA first retrieves the merchant’s KYC record from the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR) with consent, following the prescribed process. Where that record is unavailable or inaccessible under the permitted circumstances, other mechanisms under the RBI KYC Master Direction apply.


Sub-merchant KYC requirements go well beyond GST registration, where applicable. This includes[PAN verification](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/check-pan-card-details/) , applicable identity and business documents, background checks and ownership/signatory verification. Additionally, the[correct merchant category codes (MCC)](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/merchant-category-code-mcc-meaning-list-examples/) are required.


However, smaller merchants may have a less intensive process. For merchants with an annual turnover of up to ₹40 lakh or annual export turnover of up to ₹5 lakh, an alternative route requires PAN/Form 60, PAN verification, contact point verification (CPV), and a certified copy of one officially valid document for the proprietor or person holding power of attorney to operate the account, as applicable. The prescribed business document or equivalent e-document must also be verified. This alternative applies in the circumstances described above. CPV means physical verification of the address or place of business. It is not a KYC exemption.


Non-bank PAs can utilize agents for identity checks, which can include digital KYC and assisted Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP). However, agents can only be utilized for limited purposes, and the PA remains liable for conducting the necessary due diligence.


Existing merchants onboarded through December 31, 2025, had to comply with these requirements within one year of the September 15, 2025 Master Direction, by September 15, 2026. This is an elapsed transition deadline, not an additional year available to merchants now.


##


How Business Type Influences Sub-Merchant KYC Documents


All sub-merchants do not undergo the same level of due diligence. The nature of documentation collected depends on the nature of the business.


Our merchant onboarding flow uses the fourth letter of a merchant’s PAN to determine their business type. ‘P’ indicates that it is either an Individual/Proprietorship firm; ‘C’ represents both Public and[Private Limited Company](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/private-limited-company-explained/) ; ‘F’ represents Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) / Partnership Firm.


When a proprietor submits an application, they typically provide PAN, Aadhaar verification and bank details in the supported flow. When a company applies for registration, apart from providing PAN, CIN and bank details, it would also be required to submit GSTIN if it has obtained registration under GST. Additionally, when determining whether to require additional documentation to support the RBI compliance requirements, the size and nature of the merchant are also taken into consideration. The alternative process for qualifying smaller merchants does not remove the applicable verification requirements.


##


How a Merchant Onboarding API Works


A merchant onboarding API allows your platform to onboard sub-merchants directly through your own product. One example of how this is done is through our[embedded merchant onboarding flow](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/partners/embedded/embedded-merchant-onboarding) :


1. **Create merchant** : Send core details (contact email, business details, website policy URLs, bank account and signatory) through the[Create Merchant API](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/api-reference/platforms/latest/merchant-onboarding/create-merchant) , and store the merchant ID.
2. **Update details** : Add information such as GSTIN and CIN. The majority of profile fields become locked via API after activation, therefore complete these accurately beforehand.
3. **Upload KYC docs:** Accepted document types include PAN, Aadhaar,[GSTIN](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-goods-and-service-tax-identification-number/) , CIN and bank statements. The required documents depend on the merchant’s profile.
4. **Generate onboarding link:** The merchant uses the[embeddable onboarding link](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/api-reference/platforms/latest/merchant-onboarding/create-embeddable-onboarding-link-does-not-require-login) to complete the remaining KYC and Aadhaar verification. The link becomes invalid after 60 minutes; include it in an iframe or webview instead of sharing it as a plain URL.
5. **Monitor status** : Track` CREATED` ,` ACTIVE` ,` REJECTED` and` SUSPENDED` statuses. Creating a profile does not mean the merchant is active.
6. **Webhook subscription** : When there is a change in status, an[onboarding webhook](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/api-reference/platforms/latest/merchant-onboarding/webhooks) is triggered; always verify its signature before acting upon it.


This entire workflow may be tested through a sandbox environment prior to going live.


##


Benefits of Embedded Onboarding for Your Platform


Merchant journeys away from your platform to register with a third-party[payment service provider (PSP)](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/payment-service-provider/) can add friction. Merchant journeys for KYC are completed within your platform by using embedded onboarding; therefore, you can track the status of applications at all stages of the process. Embedded onboarding also reduces the burden of developing every part of payments infrastructure internally, which would include managing onboarding processes for merchants, integrating vendors, processing checkouts, reconciliation and operational controls. By utilizing an embedded model of onboarding, you build integrations one time and develop capabilities to support more eligible merchants under the agreed programme. Your platform still needs secure data handling, reliable integration and clear support responsibilities.


##


Sub-Merchant Onboarding Checks to Complete Before Going Live


**Don’t just consider PayFac as a licence:** while being labeled as a global PayFac doesn’t define your legal requirements for doing business in India; you still have to abide by Indian law.


**Be thorough when collecting data:** once a merchant’s account has been activated most fields cannot be edited via API. So, if some data was incorrect at first registration you’ll encounter problems downstream when verifying this information.


**Embed Cashfree onboarding links within your product:** The embeddable link expires after one hour. Do not send it via email or messaging applications, or expose it to end users as a direct URL.


**Validate webhook signatures before processing events:** Check the merchant and status details as well, so unauthorised or mismatched events do not change your onboarding state.


**Do not forget existing merchants:** Confirm that merchants onboarded prior to 2026 completed the applicable transition requirements. Continue monitoring changes to ownership, business activity and risk after activation.


##


How Cashfree Supports Sub-Merchant Onboarding and Payments


We are an RBI-authorised payment aggregator. Our[Embedded Payments](https://www.cashfree.com/embedded-payments/) solution enables platform providers to onboard additional businesses and offer payments within their software.


Platform providers are able to onboard sub-businesses using defined or customisable flow processes, with KYC/compliance checks performed for each merchant. Activation follows verification and approval. After a sub-merchant is onboarded, each is managed through a[partner dashboard](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/partners/embedded/dashboard) where the partner is able to view payment information and any applicable commissions.

Product availability and setup depend on the approved use case; a split-settlement vendor is not automatically the same as an Embedded Payments merchant.


##


Conclusion


Sub-merchant onboarding is the beginning of the entire payment process for your sub-businesses. The choice of payment aggregator model you utilize, RBI’s KYC requirements and the ability to build an end-to-end payment processing experience into your application through the use of a merchant onboarding API are what ultimately dictate how quickly your merchants become live and how well your platform remains compliant.

FAQs


#### What is sub-merchant onboarding?


Onboarding of sub-merchants is the process of confirming and activating those businesses that accept payments through a payment aggregation platform or other similar arrangement. In a PayFac programme, this generally differs from accepting payments directly through their own direct merchant account. Identity checks, risk assessment and approval precede live payment acceptance.


#### Who is a sub-merchant?


A sub-merchant is an independent third-party entity that collects payments through a platform or payment provider’s arrangements. Typically there will be a unique identifier assigned to each sub-merchant that can be used for both reporting and settlement purposes. The precise contractual relationship depends on the programme; merchants onboarded through Cashfree’s embedded flow are registered in our system and linked to the platform’s partner account.


#### What documents are necessary for sub-merchant KYC?


Business PAN, applicable officially valid documents for the proprietor or relevant account operator, bank details, and business documentation such as GSTIN or CIN may be required. Smaller merchants that report up to ₹40 lakh annually may qualify for the alternative due diligence route described above. The checklist depends on the entity and route; simpler onboarding does not mean automatic approval.


#### Are payment facilitators and payment aggregators the same?


No. Payment facilitator is a card-network programme role, while payment aggregator is a regulated category in India under the RBI. A provider may perform overlapping functions, subject to its authorisations, network arrangements and contracts.


#### Do platforms need their own PA authorisation to onboard merchants?


Platforms can partner with an RBI-authorised payment aggregator for embedded onboarding and payments. Whether a platform needs separate authorisation depends on the regulated activities it performs and how it handles funds. An API integration or partnership does not, by itself, determine that position.
